summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-babel-use@13.2.7 preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package presents itself as an ESLint configuration but ships a preinstall hook that runs on `npm install`. `package.json` declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. `setup.mjs` is obfuscated with hex-named identifiers and downloads the Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, extracts it, chmods it executable, then uses `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js` under Bun. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line obfuscated blob (rotated string-array via `push(shift())`, hex-named identifiers, encoded byte tables) with no documented purpose and no connection to ESLint rule configuration. The combination — alternate-runtime dropper (fetching Bun so Node-based tooling does not execute the payload) plus an undeclared obfuscated payload run automatically at install — is a supply-chain compromise pattern. Version 13.2.7 is absent from the upstream CHANGELOG (which jumps from 13.2.0 to 13.2.7), consistent with a hijacked release in the `@ornikar` scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
